question: Yamini Krishnamurthy is famous for which dance form?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mungara Yamini Krishnamurthy**, an **Indian dancer **who specialises in **Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam**, was born on December 20, 1940.
 
• In **Madras, Yamini Krishnamurthy** made his debut in 1957.
 
• She is honoured to serve as the **Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam's Asthana Nartaki** (resident dancer).
 
• She was also referred to as the "**torch bearer**" of the **Kuchipudi dancing style.**
 
• The **Padma Shree** (1968), **Padma Bhushan** (2001), and **Padma Vibhushan** (2016), three of the highest civilian honours bestowed by the **Republic of India**, were among the many honours she received for her dancing career.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri**

 
 
• **​**The state's official language is Meitei (also known as **Manipuri**). It is a recognised language of the **Republic** of India and is widely spoken in the **Manipur** region.
 
• Like most of **Northeast India, Manipur** has a significant amount of **linguistic** **diversity** in addition to Meitei.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• **​**A significant ancient Indian classical dance, known as **Odissi** or **Orissi** in older writings, has its roots in the temples of **Odisha**, an eastern coastal state of India.
 
• In the past, **Odissi** was primarily performed by women, and it used songs that were written and created in accordance with the ragas and talas of the music to express religious stories and spiritual ideals, notably those of **Vaishnavism**.
 
 
 
• **Yakshagana**
 
 
• ​In the districts of **Dakshina** **Kannada**, **Udupi, Uttara Kannada, Shimoga,** and the **western** portion of **Chikmagalur** in the state of **Karnataka**, as well as in **Kasaragod** district in the state of **Kerala**, **yakshagaana** is a traditional theatre that combines dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up, and stage techniques in a distinctive style and form.
 
• It is thought to have developed from pre-classical theatre and music during the **Bhakti** movement.
